title: Targeted Re-Collection: Calendar-Bug Heal
summary: Healed the 142 flag_missing_event_day (calendar_bug) events and 1,849 flag_window_calendar_bug window-damaged events via targeted vendor re-fetch. Two amendments: Amendment 1 replaced a too-strict archive-schema-equality gate with content-equivalence (optional sparse fields NULL-fillable); Amendment 2 added a standing pre-insertion collision guard after discovering trades/quotes collection can fail independently, and remediated one already-inserted duplicate (SDOT). Final: 149/150 event-days and 1,832/1,849 window-damage events healed/resolved; universe 20,802 -> 20,951. Trades-only quote-gap hard boundary respected throughout - never touched.

surprises: Phase 1b's original per-offset damage labeling overcounted: ATER 2022-04-13 was flagged with 2 damaged offsets but only 1 was a real gap - the other date was already correctly archived, just at a shifted legacy-window position.
Trades and quotes collection for a calendar-bug session can fail independently - 10 events (SDOT, SHMD, and all 8 T5 'unknowns') had quotes already present while trades were genuinely zero.

exchange/id/participant_timestamp/sequence_number/tape/trf_id/trf_timestamp are present in only ~84% of trades rows (absent from ~32% of a 200-file sample) - a large, previously-uncharacterized corpus split, not flagged optional (above the 1% threshold) and not investigated further.

ARBB 2024-02-13's archive trades are capped at exactly 50,000 rows (25% of the true 197,326) yet reach the identical true final timestamp - not the simple prefix-truncation pattern already documented for Group A; mechanism undetermined.
4/20 control pairs show sub-cent price-precision drift (max $0.00005), 99% concentrated on exchange=4 (FINRA/ADF TRF-reported prints).
